items.summary: We prove that a finite poset with at most fifteen elements, width at most three, and the following common-incomparability property has at most 48 antichains: for every x < y, the elements incomparable with both x and y form a chain of size at most two. An explicit fifteen-element poset attains the bound. We show that order-six stable-marriage rotation posets satisfy these hypotheses by examining convex rotation blocks and their fixed partner pools. This gives a structural upper bound of 48 stable matchings, matching the lower bound already provided by Benjamin, Converse, and Krieger in 1995. Equality forces fifteen rotations, all of size two, and every one of the 36 man–woman pairs occurs in some stable matching. Provenance note: This preprint is accompanied by reproducible verification artifacts and a partial Lean formalization. The Lean development verifies the finite-poset core and supporting components; it does not formalize the entire stable-marriage theorem f(6) = 48 end to end. The source-code and reproducibility repository is available at https://github.com/insammael/stable-marriage-f6 and is linked as a related resource.
items.title: Small Rotation Blocks and the Order-Six Stable Marriage Problem

items.summary: Abstract Distributed version control preserves source states, ancestry, branching, merging, and collaboration with extraordinary success. It does not ordinarily require engineering intent, failed approaches, claim scope, verification evidence, residual disagreement, or continuation state to exist as typed repository objects. Those records instead tend to be distributed across commit prose, review systems, issue trackers, CI logs, artifact stores, chat, and human memory. This disclosure explores a broader version-control model for software developed by humans and agents without claiming that content addressing, provenance, attestations, change-oriented versioning, or agent memory are new in isolation. Gemel models an evidence-bearing change : a content-addressed relation from an exact input state to an exact output state, linked to intent, operations, producer provenance, claims, evidence, residuals, verification scope, and causal context. Trajectories preserve completed, rejected, interrupted, superseded, and inconclusive work. Claims remain declarations rather than stored truth; support and readiness are derived conservatively from evidence, residuals, freshness, supersession, and policy. Context manifests and checkpoints provide bounded continuation surfaces without requiring private reasoning transcripts. The inspected Rust reference implementation defines deterministic canonical encoding, BLAKE3-256 identities, immutable objects, mutable refs, rebuildable indexes, 24 object families, Git-carried exchange, deterministic Git projection, semantic indexing, native and hosted synchronization, agent queries, policy checks, and an FRF court runner. For this paper, the supplied source archive was independently built in a clean temporary directory and cargo test --all-targets completed 236 tests with zero failures. This result is implementation-specific conformance evidence. It is not evidence that Gemel improves developer productivity, agent reliability, or industrial outcomes. Gemel composes with the Forensic Residual Framework (FRF) as an evidence plane and with FRF-Fuzz as a discovery plane. The paper situates that composition against Git facilities, patch algebra, provenance models, software-supply-chain attestations, reproducible builds, software archives, event sourcing, rationale capture, and agent memory. It discloses alternative embodiments and defines falsifiable evaluations for handoff quality, repeated-error reduction, evidence freshness, reconciliation, interoperability, context cost, storage overhead, and longitudinal fuzzing. Its principal claim is architectural: software history can be represented as an engineering graph in which source state, intent, evidence, residual uncertainty, negative knowledge, and continuation state possess explicit identity and scope. Whether that representation earns its operational cost remains an empirical question. Keywords distributed version control; Git; agentic software development; evidence engineering; provenance; content addressing; Merkle DAG; software agents; developmental trajectories; negative knowledge; residual primacy; FRF; FRF-Fuzz; reproducibility; software archaeology; semantic lineage; source provenance; event sourcing.
items.title: Gemel: Evidence-Native Version Control for Agentic Software Development - Longitudinal Engineering Memory, Residual-Aware Change Graphs, Git Interchange, and Reproducible Agent Handoffs

items.summary: Research and educational instrument. Not for clinical use, for the care of any patient, or to determine or influence any drug dose. A simulation-calibrated informatics pipeline that fits a single-compartment exponential approximation to published population pharmacokinetic models of unfractionated heparin during cardiopulmonary bypass, and renders the result as an institution-specific decay nomogram. This is the supporting code and archived analysis for manuscript JCVA-D-26-01511. Published models of heparin disposition are biexponential and require a computer to evaluate. The pipeline asks how well a single decay constant k — calibrated to an institution's own dosing, weight and bypass-time distributions — can approximate a chosen reference model, and quantifies where it fails. The answer differs sharply by model: at the reversal timepoint the approximation holds to 0.38% mean absolute error for Lanoiselée and 0.44% for Jia, but to 10.3% for Delavenne, rising to 72% after repeated supplemental boluses. Contents. Five reference-model implementations with their published parameters and provenance; seeded cohort sampling and calibration; agreement statistics; nomogram geometry and rendering; a Streamlit dashboard; an automated test suite; and a frozen analysis run comprising 20 result tables, the main-text and supplementary figures, a run manifest and a manuscript-ready summary. A sixth model (PRODOSE-2) is implemented and tested but withheld from the active pipeline pending validation and peer review. Reproduction. Every reported number regenerates from one seeded command: pip install -r requirements-frozen.txt python run_analysis.py --seed 20260912 --outdir /tmp/check python check_frozen.py /tmp/check All randomness comes from explicitly seeded generators, each analysis stage drawing from its own independent stream. Re-running reproduces every archived result to within floating-point rounding on any machine, and byte-for-byte on the machine the archive was built on. The manifest records the seed, the commit, the package versions and every analysis decision. Continuous integration runs the suite on two Python versions, each test file again in isolation, and the reproduction check on every push. Verification, and its limits. Automated checks confirm that each closed-form solution actually solves its own differential equations and satisfies the identities they imply, and six landmark values from a published simulation are reproduced to within 3%. No participant-level data from any source study is held, so no model is re-fitted and no prediction is compared with an observation. What is demonstrated is faithful implementation of the published models — not that the published models are correct. No external or predictive validation is claimed. Scope. The pipeline represents the pharmacokinetic central-compartment amount only. It does not model the pharmacodynamic layer — anti-factor Xa activity or activated clotting time — nor peripheral-compartment heparin, antithrombin, protamine pharmacology or heparin rebound. Converting a residual amount into a protamine dose requires an institutional ratio that this software does not supply. Intended purpose. This software is a research and educational instrument whose purpose is to demonstrate and teach an informatics method under simulated conditions. Within that intended purpose it is not a medical device. items.summary: A three-signal stopping rule for iterative LLM refinement derived from the Möbius theory stack: an equilibrium-distance surrogate d̂_R (RZGM meaning-equilibrium layer), an update-free-recurrence and diversity-collapse detector pair (Reflective Homeostasis Layer), and a hard reflection-depth cap (MUSE bounded reflection). Pre-registered study: 500 English prose-refinement tasks across ten domains, two generator models (Gemma4 12B-IT-QAT and 26B-A4B-IT-QAT), 8,000 generations, 999 blind position-swapped pairwise judgments. The governor cuts refinement tokens by 36.6% / 33.1% (bootstrap 95% CIs 33.6-39.5% / 30.3-35.9%) versus an always-eight-iterations baseline — 2.2-3.4x a naive convergence stop — at a measured quality cost reported at equal prominence: 38.0% / 36.6% of judged comparisons lost overall, a majority among actual interventions (61.1% / 59.0%), with measured cost almost perfectly collinear with output length. items.summary: We present an HTTP threat detection system embedded in a production reverse proxy that achieves sub-500ns per-request inference latency. The system combines a depth-limited CART decision tree with a compact two-layer MLP in an ensemble architecture, where the tree provides fast-path classification and the MLP refines uncertain cases. Model weights are exported as Rust `const` arrays, enabling zero-allocation deployment with no runtime deserialization. We formalize structural safety properties of the ensemble in the Lean~4 theorem prover, establishing a three-tier verification approach covering structural invariants, weight-dependent decision bounds, and floating-point error propagation. In initial small-scale trials on a combined dataset of production logs, CSIC-2010, and CIC-IDS2017-derived features, the ensemble achieves >99% validation accuracy for both scanner and DDoS detection, with tree inference completing in under 2ns and full ensemble inference under 6ns. We discuss limitations of the current training data and outline directions for scaling to larger, human-labeled corpora.
items.title: Sub-Microsecond HTTP Threat Detection with Decision Tree–MLP Ensembles and Lean 4 Verification

items.summary: This manuscript identifies six substrates — individual memory, species lineages, externalised records, immune memory, the first generation of stars, and prion populations — which share a four-part mechanical structure, and among which no pair, to our knowledge, cites another. We specify the four mechanisms as an explicit screen, and validate it by applying it to cases that should fail: thermal equilibrium scores zero of four, sheared amorphous matter scores an intermediate two and a half, and stem cells score three of four in a manner that identifies precisely which mechanism is missing. We then derive, from this framework’s own commitment that any render of a record is necessarily partial, a scaling law governing all six: the more degraded the record, the more the reconstruction is determined by the template rather than by the record. We show this law is independently confirmed in four of the six fields, under four different names, by researchers not addressing one another. We supply a birth term that a companion manuscript’s earlier treatment lacked, deriving it from Bennett’s history-tape result rather than from biology, and show that a standard macroevolutionary survivorship formula then applies to memory unchanged. Three results that did not hold are recorded in full, including one prediction that failed outright on simulation and one correspondence that was stated backwards relative to the data. The foundational architecture, geometric intuitions, and motivating philosophy of this framework originated independently with the author prior to and separate from any AI involvement. Subsequent mathematical derivation, connection to established physics literature, computational verification, and error-checking were conducted through extended technical work with AI systems (Anthropic’s Claude and Google’s Gemini). The author directed this process, evaluated and selected among proposed derivations, and takes full responsibility for the accuracy and originality of the final work.
items.title: Reconstruction from a Degraded Record: Six Substrates, One Scaling Law, and a Dispute Six Fields Have Independently

items.summary: Anticoncentration is a key ingredient in complexity theoretic arguments for quantum advantage from Gaussian boson sampling. Here we prove polynomial small ball anticoncentration for complex Gaussian transpose Gram hafnians and complex symmetric Gaussian hafnians. For a k × 2n matrix X with independent standard complex Gaussian entries, we establish polynomial small ball anticoncentration for haf(XᵀX) under k ≥ 4n and n²/k = O(log n). For hafnians of 2n × 2n complex symmetric Gaussian matrices, polynomial small ball anticoncentration holds for every n ≥ 1. In both ensembles, any prescribed inverse polynomial failure probability can be achieved with an inverse polynomial small ball radius, uniformly over all centers. These results go beyond moment based anticoncentration by controlling the probability of small hafnian amplitudes. The proof combines Fourier compression with conditional Wishart geometry to handle dependent hafnian cofactors. Files: main.pdf contains the main article (14 pages); supplement.pdf contains the supplementary proofs and additional results (33 pages). Related Lean verification sources: https://doi.org/10.5281/zenodo.22554594 and https://github.com/HongruZhao/ComplexGramHafnians.
items.title: Local Anticoncentration for Gaussian Boson Sampling via Conditional Wishart Geometry

items.summary: Within the Complementarity-First and Reciprocal Internal Complementarity research program, we study regular perturbations of a supplied smooth massive degree-one SU(2) Yang–Mills–Higgs monopole with equal scalar and vector masses. A neutral transverse readout satisfies an exact nonlinear equation whose source is a divergence of an L2 tensor plus an L6/5 remainder. An additional affine infrared class is preserved on compact regular intervals and transported to admitted framed gauge and collective charts. Ordinary kinetic collective subtraction need not preserve its homogeneous negative norm; a compensating sum retains the relevant cancellation. Pure spatial transport is skew, while complete coordinate corrections admit an endpoint Duhamel identity. These statements concern finite-time admissibility, not uniform all-time localization. Assuming the companion’s nonnegative physical Hessian, complete framed kernel, local-moment coercivity and explicit threshold-packet estimates, a Gauss projection of a compact weighted translation yields a sharper test in the same monopole background. Its affine tail label differs from its actual initial local center rate, and its collective-orthogonal velocity lies outside the domain of the physical Hessian’s inverse square root. Its global linearized local-moment connection residual is unbounded in kinetic L2 while remaining bounded in the energy norm. We obtain an exponentially weighted time-average lower bound, not a universal pointwise growth law. Fixed-time differentiability excludes a time-uniform linear-scale nonlinear strong-residual estimate on this class, but does not establish nonlinear Lyapunov instability. The actual spectral inverse-square-root domain is necessary and sufficient for bounded unforced linear radiative position. We identify the nonlinear physical source that would need stronger control. The example proves that affine admissibility does not imply spectral admissibility; it does not classify their full inclusion relation or prove all-time nonlinear spectral propagation.

items.summary: Science communication poster and educational resource developed for the 2026 European Researchers’ Night–Nit de la Investigació at the University of Alicante as supporting material for a hands-on activity devoted to coin production. For this activity, an enlarged minting system based on the dies of a silver Carthaginian shekel has been reproduced by means of 3D printing. Participants can directly experience how hammered coinage works by placing a modelling-clay flan between a fixed lower die and a movable upper die, and observing how pressure impresses the obverse and reverse types onto its surface. The poster provides the historical and technological context for this activity through an overview of the evolution of coin production and means of payment, from manual hammered coinage to the mechanisation of coin manufacture and contemporary digital payment systems. It presents in a synthetic way some of the main technological developments, including hammered coinage, mechanised roller minting, the screw press, banknote production and security features, and the progressive dematerialisation of payment methods. Developed within the framework of the PArchTE ( Predictive Archaeology and Transition Economies ) and SEDES (PID2023-152305NB-I00) projects. The activity forms part of “UA Divulga VI. Annual Plan of the UCC+i of the University of Alicante (2025–2026)” (FCT-24-20347), funded by the Spanish Foundation for Science and Technology (FECYT). Activity developed by the University Institute for Research in Archaeology and Historical Heritage (INAPH), University of Alicante.

items.summary: Abstract Distributed version control preserves source states, ancestry, branching, merging, and collaboration with extraordinary success. It does not ordinarily require engineering intent, failed approaches, claim scope, verification evidence, residual disagreement, or continuation state to exist as typed repository objects. Those records instead tend to be distributed across commit prose, review systems, issue trackers, CI logs, artifact stores, chat, and human memory. This disclosure explores a broader version-control model for software developed by humans and agents without claiming that content addressing, provenance, attestations, change-oriented versioning, or agent memory are new in isolation. Gemel models an evidence-bearing change : a content-addressed relation from an exact input state to an exact output state, linked to intent, operations, producer provenance, claims, evidence, residuals, verification scope, and causal context. Trajectories preserve completed, rejected, interrupted, superseded, and inconclusive work. Claims remain declarations rather than stored truth; support and readiness are derived conservatively from evidence, residuals, freshness, supersession, and policy. Context manifests and checkpoints provide bounded continuation surfaces without requiring private reasoning transcripts. The inspected Rust reference implementation defines deterministic canonical encoding, BLAKE3-256 identities, immutable objects, mutable refs, rebuildable indexes, 24 object families, Git-carried exchange, deterministic Git projection, semantic indexing, native and hosted synchronization, agent queries, policy checks, and an FRF court runner. For this paper, the supplied source archive was independently built in a clean temporary directory and cargo test --all-targets completed 236 tests with zero failures. This result is implementation-specific conformance evidence. It is not evidence that Gemel improves developer productivity, agent reliability, or industrial outcomes. Gemel composes with the Forensic Residual Framework (FRF) as an evidence plane and with FRF-Fuzz as a discovery plane. The paper situates that composition against Git facilities, patch algebra, provenance models, software-supply-chain attestations, reproducible builds, software archives, event sourcing, rationale capture, and agent memory. It discloses alternative embodiments and defines falsifiable evaluations for handoff quality, repeated-error reduction, evidence freshness, reconciliation, interoperability, context cost, storage overhead, and longitudinal fuzzing. Its principal claim is architectural: software history can be represented as an engineering graph in which source state, intent, evidence, residual uncertainty, negative knowledge, and continuation state possess explicit identity and scope. Whether that representation earns its operational cost remains an empirical question. items.summary: Anticoncentration is a key ingredient in complexity theoretic arguments for quantum advantage from Gaussian boson sampling. Here we prove polynomial small ball anticoncentration for complex Gaussian transpose Gram hafnians and complex symmetric Gaussian hafnians. For a k × 2n matrix X with independent standard complex Gaussian entries, we establish polynomial small ball anticoncentration for haf(XᵀX) under k ≥ 4n and n²/k = O(log n). For hafnians of 2n × 2n complex symmetric Gaussian matrices, polynomial small ball anticoncentration holds for every n ≥ 1. In both ensembles, any prescribed inverse polynomial failure probability can be achieved with an inverse polynomial small ball radius, uniformly over all centers. These results go beyond moment based anticoncentration by controlling the probability of small hafnian amplitudes. The proof combines Fourier compression with conditional Wishart geometry to handle dependent hafnian cofactors. Files: main.pdf contains the main article (14 pages); supplement.pdf contains the supplementary proofs and additional results (33 pages). Related Lean verification sources: https://doi.org/10.5281/zenodo.22554594 and https://github.com/HongruZhao/ComplexGramHafnians.

items.summary: This paper refines the finiteness conjecture for stability architectures and establishes the strongest currently provable results. A stability claim is treated as a profile specifying the object, state space, evolution, perturbation class, projection, failure region, time horizon, and obstructing gap or invariant. An architecture abstracts the structural core: the category of state spaces, the operator class, the gap functional, and the transport obstruction. The paper proves that stability cannot be classified from the trajectory map alone; the full profile matters. For linear systems, there are exactly three distinct architectures: dissipative, geometric or gradient, and Hamiltonian. For model-theoretic stability, the classification is finite and known: stability, NIP, simplicity, and rosiness. This logical classification is an analogy, not a direct translation to dynamics. For Hamiltonian systems, conditional finiteness identifies five candidate mechanisms: KAM persistence, Nekhoroshev confinement, Trojan resonance-gap suppression, symmetry constraint, and barrier obstruction. For statistical systems, four candidates appear: uniform, partial, and non-uniform hyperbolicity, plus rate conditions. In both cases, finiteness follows only if the lists are exhaustive, which remains conjectural. The paper also proves an intra-architecture transfer theorem, a qualified cross-architecture rigidity theorem, and a proposition on overlapping architectures. Transfer works within a shared architecture because estimates depend only on structural data. Rigidity blocks transfer between structurally distinct architectures unless additional structure exists. Overlap is possible, allowing multiple stability mechanisms and multiple failure routes. The general classification problem is undecidable, proved by reduction from the halting problem. Limitations include autonomous, finite-dimensional, smooth dynamics; time-dependent, infinite-dimensional, non-smooth, and nonlinear cases remain open. The consequences concern analog laboratories, engineering design by architecture selection, and a finite core of stability theory. The central message is that the finiteness conjecture is not vacuous: it holds where testable, while full generality awaits resolution of the exhaustiveness conjectures.
items.title: Stability Architectures: A Finite Classification of Provable Cases

items.summary: This paper asks a narrow question. Lyapunov stability, geometric stability, and statistical stability are all described as spectral-gap properties. The gaps act on different operators, live on different spaces, and survive different perturbations. The informal habit of treating them as one nested hierarchy is correct for convex wells and hyperbolic sinks. It is not correct as a statement about dynamical systems in general. The paper replaces that habit with a comparison theorem. A stability claim is a profile: an evolution, a perturbation class, a projection, and a failure set. Comparative type can change when the map is held fixed and only the projection changes. Three statistical properties are kept distinct. The first is weak continuity of an invariant measure under perturbation. The second is a spectral gap of a transfer or Fokker–Planck operator on a named function space. The third is differentiability of the measure in the perturbation parameter. These three can hold together. They can also separate. The proved implications are scoped. A positive Hessian implies Lyapunov stability of a mechanical equilibrium and a dissipative Jacobian gap for a gradient flow. A hyperbolic sink gives weak continuity of a Dirac family and does not give mixing on a positive-dimensional density space. Uniform hyperbolicity gives a transfer-operator gap on an anisotropic space and, in the perturbation class of Keller and Liverani, weak continuity of an SRB family. Partial hyperbolicity yields a gap only after restriction to the hyperbolic factor. Nonuniform hyperbolicity with a Young tower yields a slower, tail-controlled rate and is compatible with instability of almost every orbit. A prescribed decay for a piecewise expanding map or a hypocoercive generator need not come from any hyperbolic splitting. Architectural estimates do not transfer between structurally distinct operator classes. In one linear-quadratic noise model the three classical tests return the same number. In a double well they separate. The paper does not claim that statistical mechanisms are finite, and it does not prove that averaging a frequency-gap Hamiltonian system produces a kinetic spectral gap.
items.title: Which Spectral Gaps Imply Which: Lyapunov, Geometric, and Statistical Criteria

items.summary: README – Coarse-Grained Molecular Dynamics (CGMD) Simulations of PIEZO1 and TRPM4 Overview This dataset contains coarse-grained molecular dynamics (CGMD) simulations of the mechanosensitive ion channel PIEZO1 and the non-mechanoprotective ion channel TRPM4 embedded in lipid bilayers. The simulations comprise 500 ns of equilibrium followed by membrane stretching simulations designed to investigate how PIEZO1's distinctive triskelion blade architecture redistributes mechanical stress and preserves membrane integrity. All simulations were performed using GROMACS with the Martini 3 force field. Independent replicate simulations (n = 3) were conducted for each system to ensure statistical robustness and reproducibility. Simulation Details Parameter Description Molecular dynamics engine : GROMACS v2021.2 Force field : Martini 3 Membrane model : Lipid bilayer containing either PIEZO1 or TRPM4 Equilibration : 500 ns Stretching simulations : Three independent replicates (n = 3); 50 ns Simulation temperature, pressure, and all additional parameters are provided in the accompanying simulation input files (.mdp) and described in the associated publication. Biological Significance PIEZO1 is a mechanosensitive ion channel whose unique triskelion blade architecture protects cellular membranes from mechanical failure. Its extended peripheral blades redistribute mechanical stress across the lipid bilayer, reducing localized stress accumulation and delaying membrane rupture during mechanical loading. This dataset enables quantitative investigation of how membrane protein architecture influences membrane mechanics, force redistribution, and mechanoprotection using coarse-grained molecular dynamics simulations. Dataset Structure 1. Equilibrium Simulations These simulations characterize the equilibrated membrane environment surrounding each ion channel before mechanical loading. Simulation length: 500 ns PIEZO1_equilibrium.pdb PIEZO1_equilibrium.xtc TRPM4_equilibrium.pdb TRPM4_equilibrium.xtc 2. Membrane Stretching Simulations Following equilibration, membrane stretch was induced using semi-isotropic pressure coupling, with −5 bar applied in the membrane plane (x–y) while maintaining +1 bar normal to the bilayer (z-axis) using the Parrinello–Rahman barostat. items.summary: ElectromagneticFields v0.9.0 Diff since v0.8.0 Breaking Changes Everything here that requires a change to calling code, and what to do about it. The sections below give the reasoning; this is the checklist. @code , its seven per-preset variants, code and load_equilibrium are gone. Generated code is no longer injected into a module. Build a field by calling FieldFunctions(equ) , which returns a value: it can be constructed inside a function, stored, and passed to a vector field through a problem's parameters , none of which the old module injection allowed. The ~450 scalar functions are ~41 generics returning tensors, each taking the field first. B¹(t, q) becomes B♯(field, t, q)[1] and dAᵢdxⱼ(t, q) becomes DA♭(field, t, q)[i, j] . The names use the musical isomorphisms — ♭ covariant, ♯ contravariant, ♮ physical, the bare letter the magnitude — and Changed below has the full old-to-new table. Every one of the ~444 old scalar values is an entry of one of the new tensors. The per-field submodules are flattened into the package. Solovev.ITER() is SolovevEquilibriumITER() , ThetaPinch.init() is ThetaPinchEquilibrium() , and so on for every field; Solovev.ITER(xpoint = true) and its siblings are gone in favour of the named X-point constructors. The coordinate helpers X , Y , Z , R , r , θ , ϕ and r² are package-level generics and deliberately not exported — reach them as ElectromagneticFields.R or through coordinates(field) . periodicity is no longer answered or exported by this package. GeometricBase.periodic(equ) gives one Bool per coordinate instead, and a chart with no method for it raises a MethodError when a field is built from it, deliberately. Code that assembled a (xmin, xmax) tuple from rangemin / rangemax behind a single flag must now build it from periodic and the bounds. periodicity = periodic(field) is silently wrong , not an error: a three-element Bool vector destructures to (false, false) . parameters(field) for a Solov'ev equilibrium now includes the coefficient vector c . A₃ reads it, so it travels with the other parameters instead of being frozen into the code. A field rebuilt after clear_field_cache!() is equal to a few ULP, not bit for bit. Compare two builds of one field with a tolerance rather than == . SymEngine is no longer a dependency ; Symbolics, StaticArrays, GeometricBase and ConstructionBase are. The Julia floor stays 1.10. Added Aqua.jl runs as part of the test suite , in test/aqua_tests.jl , which calls Aqua.test_all . This package carried no package-level quality check of any kind before, so all eight — method ambiguities, unbound type parameters, undefined exports, the agreement between Project.toml and test/Project.toml , stale dependencies, [compat] bounds, type piracy and persistent tasks — start from a clean pass rather than from a list of known failures. items.summary: This paper offers a critical analysis of the European Union as a model of regional integration and examines its contribution to peace and to the effectiveness of the United Nations system. Set against the background of the failure of the League of Nations, the study argues that the post-1945 international order has endured largely because it is supported by strong regional institutions. Using the EU as the primary case study, the paper contends that by institutionalizing peace within Europe through economic interdependence, binding law, and supranational governance, the EU has created a zone of stability that reduces the burden on global governance structures. Furthermore, the paper analyzes how the EU functions as a support pillar for the United Nations under Chapter VIII of the UN Charter. Through financial contributions, peacekeeping partnerships, and coordinated diplomacy, the EU has reinforced multilateralism and provided capacity for conflict management and development. A comparative perspective is also drawn with other regional bodies such as ECOWAS to demonstrate a broader pattern of regional-global cooperation. The paper concludes that the longevity of the United Nations, compared to the League of Nations, can be partly explained by this two-level architecture of global and regional governance. While the EU’s support for the UN is substantial, it is also inconsistent, as internal EU divisions sometimes undermine collective action. Ultimately, the study shows that effective regional integration is a critical condition for sustaining peace and strengthening the United Nations system.
items.title: The European Union and Regional Integration: A Critical Analysis of Peacebuilding and Support for the United Nations System

items.summary: Embarrassingly parallel workloads, such as parameter sweeps, Monte Carlo simulations, and hyperparameter searches, are pervasive in research computing, yet running a single experiment across a mix of laptops, lab servers, cloud virtual machines (VMs), and high-performance computing (HPC) clusters still demands ad hoc Secure Shell (SSH) tunnels, port forwarding, and scheduler-specific scripts. We present DART, a job distributor that turns any such mix of machines into a single shared queue. DART pairs a Dockerized job server with a one-line worker command-line interface (CLI); a hosted Hub automates reverse tunneling, worker authentication, and public endpoint provisioning, so collaborators on any network, including those behind network address translation (NAT) or using a personal laptop, can join an experiment with a single API-key and no firewall changes. This makes DART especially effective for researchers who combine Advanced Cyberinfrastructure Coordination Ecosystem: Services & Support (ACCESS)-provisioned HPC resources [1] with institutional clusters and personal workstations, federating all resources under one queue with no per-site configuration. All communication is encrypted end-to-end, and access is controlled through API-key authentication and a personal identification number (PIN)-protected dashboard. Researchers create experiments, define parameter grids, and monitor jobs entirely from a web dashboard; a work-conserving scheduler dispatches jobs on demand, exploits resource heterogeneity, and automatically re-queues failures. In a real-world deployment of 37,720 jobs across 68 heterogeneous machines spanning an institutional HPC cluster, a national ACCESS resource, and personal computers, the observed run completed in approximately eight days. DART’s dynamic allocation achieved a simulation-derived 35× speedup over static partitioning (≈4 days vs. ≈139 days), reducing a multi-month workload to days.
items.title: DART: Distributed Assignment of Research Tasks for Heterogeneous Compute Environments

Based on the above findings, it was concluded that audit quality in the Nigerian banking sector is not uniformly effective, rather, its effect on bank failure risks is selective, with only specific audit mechanisms demonstrating the capacity to significantly enhance financial solvency, thereby suggesting that the effectiveness of external audit as a safeguard against bank failure risks depend not merely on its presence, but likely on factors such as depth, credibility, and functional execution of its key components.   this study concluded that audit.  Consequently, this study recommended among others, that listed deposit money banks in Nigeria, alongside regulators and external auditors, should prioritize substantive governance quality, auditor competence and independence, rigorous audit execution, timely financial reporting, risk-sensitive audit remuneration, coordinated assurance mechanisms, and proactive internal control systems over mere procedural compliance, in order to strengthen transparency, reinforce market confidence, and enhance long term financial stability in line with Agency theory. items.summary: This technical note investigates whether operator-relative noncentrality can predict the relative empirical power of complementary localized scan statistics in correlated spectra. The motivating real-data benchmark compares BABAR and BESIII measurements of the e⁺e⁻ → π⁺π⁻ cross section in the ρ-resonance region on a common 5 MeV grid from 0.600 to 0.880 GeV. The real-data comparison remains negative, with no statistically supported localized shape tension identified. The methodological study compares a coherent-yield scan with a covariance-profiled shape scan and defines the frozen coordinate Θ = log(ES/EY), where ES and EY represent maximum local operator-accessible signal strengths. An archival confirmatory replication used 50,000 null calibration draws per covariance environment, 15,000 independent null-validation draws per environment, 1,440 signal/covariance conditions, and 576,000 injected pseudoexperiments. Θ predicted which scan had greater empirical power with pooled AUC 0.9820 and mean leave-one-covariance-environment-out AUC 0.9740; its correlation with the empirical power difference was 0.9185. Independent Type-I error estimates ranged from 0.0466 to 0.0540. The results support operator-relative noncentrality as a useful empirical coordinate for complementary globally calibrated scans within the tested benchmark. The underlying ingredients, including Gaussian noncentrality, covariance-weighted subspace detection, quadratic scanning, and Monte Carlo calibration, are established; the contribution is a reproducible computational synthesis and controlled characterization rather than a claim of a new general statistical law

items.summary: Hashing Is Not Retrieval is a prospectively frozen three-arm evaluation of context accumulation in small-model multi-agent code cartography. It compares three ways for an orchestrator to hand work to a worker: 1. FULL HISTORY — retransmit prior worker outputs. 2. OPAQUE REF — replace the previous output with an unretrievable SHA-256 digest. 3. RETRIEVED — resolve the digest through a tenant-scoped content-addressed store and inject the recovered bytes. All arms receive identical source-derived evidence. The apparatus measures the exact message content sent to workers and records token counts, model and provider identifiers, generation IDs, usage, cost, retries, and retrieval proofs. A five-task gate preceded a fixed 50-task controlled benchmark, followed by a separate state-required evaluation across 24 deterministic fixtures and a five-scale Medusa case study. Key result: in the controlled benchmark, RETRIEVED reduced paired peak context by 38.3% relative to FULL HISTORY. The state-required follow-up shows that opaque references fail when state must be recovered, while verified retrieval preserves substantially more structural information. This is bounded-context evidence for automatic orchestrator-resolved state passing inside a specific two-worker code-cartography harness — not a universal claim about autonomous memory, long-context capability, or reasoning quality. The release includes the corrected author-identified preprint, executable apparatus, frozen results, task fixtures, telemetry, and verification instructions. Version 1.0.2 supplies the curated, verifier-passing reproducibility archive. It supersedes the uncurated archive from version 1.0.1 and includes the exact pinned apparatus, state-required fixtures, frozen results, and archive verifier. items.summary: Extended reasoning can increase response time and computational cost without improving an answer. Models may revisit unproductive steps or build further reasoning on an earlier mistake. This study evaluates whether Jev, a probabilistic decision maker, can provide an inexpensive error signal to help decide when additional reasoning is needed. We compare Jev with GPT-5.6 Luna on generated ordering and logic-grid puzzles and on the official released ZebraLogic test set. The generated questions are four-choice items with one correct answer among four. The official test set is used open-ended: Luna produces the full grid, Jev checks it without the solution key, and Luna may revise once when Jev does not judge the answer consistent. On the generated multiple-choice problems, Jev is 5 to 60 percentage points more accurate than Luna with reasoning disabled, at lower measured API cost, and every observed top-choice disagreement identifies a Luna error. On a stratified sample of 200 official ZebraLogic puzzles, exact-grid accuracy rises from 41.0% with reasoning disabled to 90.5% with high-effort reasoning. A revision pass adds two points in both settings, but a revision-only control shows the gain comes from the extra attempt, not from Jev's information: on the answers Jev flags, a plain second look is at least as accurate as the Jev-informed revision (16 versus 13 correct without reasoning, and 70 versus 70 at high effort). Jev detects 93% of the weak reasoner's errors with 92% precision, but only 10% of its high-effort flags identify errors. These results motivate using Jev or similar decision models in a model harness: software that controls when to continue, reconsider, retrieve evidence, or allocate more reasoning. An early check could help avoid spending further computation on a mistaken line of reasoning. The experiments measure checking of final answers, however, and do not measure reductions in hallucination or repetitive reasoning inside a harness. On the official benchmark, extra reasoning accounts for most of the accuracy, and the checker's information does not improve on a second attempt. Larger studies with balanced answer positions, selective triggers, and step-level feedback are needed to test whether checking improves accuracy or reduces total cost.

items.summary: Self-contained synthetic seismic–gravity inversion models, Python operators, seeds, archived and profile-initialized fits, regional controls, posterior samples, figures and validation records for the manuscript by Emilson P. Leite and Maiara M. Gonçalves. Version 0.11 adds a four-start calibration on 96 paired noise comparisons, an audit of unchanged displayed seismic median errors, exact n=32 coverage intervals, and empirical bias–variance accounting of the existing regional controls. The four-start shortcut did not reproduce the profile solutions; the manuscript retains 32 profile-initialized noise pairs for each free-geometry configuration. Fixed-geometry ensembles retain 256 realizations. Wide local intervals under a free trend coexist with systematic target-property errors directed towards the prior. No new posterior chains were generated in this revision. Field observations and third-party BP-model data are not required.
